assumptions: USD million. Fictional Violet Forge group, parent and wholly owned subsidiary. Toy intra-group goods sold at fixed markup on cost; eliminate all internal sales and unrealized profit, opening unrealized profit released when sold externally. No tax.

evidence.text: [2024 inventory note] Parent sold goods to subsidiary for 120m, original cost 90m. At end2024 subsidiary retained 25% of those goods at transfer price. All these opening internal goods sold externally in2025.
[2025 internal sales] Parent sells new goods to subsidiary for 160m, original cost 120m. At closing subsidiary retains 40% at transfer price; rest sold externally. No other internal inventory.

[2025 standalone P&L]
|Entity|Revenue|COGS|Other opex|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Parent|600|400|100|
|Subsidiary|500|350|80|
[Balance] Parent ending inventory 70m, subsidiary 100m includes current internal goods at transfer price. All other inventory external origin, no NRV issue.
[Policy] Eliminate internal revenue and matching COGS 160; reduce closing inventory by unrealized profit; release prior unrealized profit to current COGS. No other consolidation adjustments.
[Draft] Analyst removes total internal sales but ignores COGS elimination, also applies current unrealized profit to full 160 rather than unsold part.

qas.question: Find prior-year unrealized intercompany profit released into 2025 COGS.
Find closing unrealized profit from the new intra-group shipment.
Reconcile consolidated external revenue.
Find consolidated COGS after elimination and both unrealized-profit movements.
Find consolidated closing inventory carrying amount.
Explain why prior-year unrealized profit enters this year's COGS as a reduction.
qas.answer: The opening inventory profit was eliminated last year; when goods sell externally this year, the prior elimination reverses so group cost reflects original external cost.

qas.question: Why does eliminating 160 internal revenue alone understate group profit?
qas.answer: The matching internal purchase/COGS must be eliminated, then only unsold internal margin remains unrealized. Eliminating just revenue double-counts group cost.

qas.question: Can the subsidiary's external gross margin on each internal product be derived?
qas.answer: No. The external sale consideration by product is not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Coral Lane retail franchisor. Toy franchisees are independent principals; franchisor earns contractual royalty and product wholesale revenue; restricted advertising fund contributions separately held as agent. All figures annual.

qas.question: Find East net franchisee customer sales for royalty calculation.
Find total earned franchise royalty under region-specific rates.
Find closing restricted advertising fund payable.
Find franchisor total recognized revenue.
Calculate franchisor operating profit excluding agency ad-fund flows.
Why should 500m franchisee net sales not be included gross in franchisor revenue?

qas.question: Reconcile whether the ad contributions create unrestricted revenue.

assumptions: USD million equivalent. Fictional Clay Brook bank. Toy contractual maturity mismatch by currency; behavioral assumptions for nonmaturity deposits explicitly given. No cross-currency transfers under stress. Cumulative cash gap includes opening free cash.

evidence.text:
[Contractual schedule]
|Currency|Opening free cash|0-30d inflows|0-30d outflows excl NMD|31-90d inflows|31-90d outflows excl NMD|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|USD|70|130|180|160|100|
|EUR equivalent|40|60|50|50|80|

[Nonmaturity deposits] USD NMD 200, EUR NMD100. Behavioral base outflow 20% of each in first30 days and additional 10% of original balance in days31–90. No outflows beyond amounts in table and NMD assumption.
[Stress] First30d NMD outflow rises to 40% of original balance in each currency; subsequent10% unchanged. No FX conversion or group transfers permitted.
[Facilities] USD committed line 25 drawable immediately; EUR committed line 10. No other available funding. Ignore interest; use lines only as needed.
[Policy] Currency-level liquidity must not go negative at each bucket end; aggregate positive cash cannot offset currency gap.
[Memo] Treasury sums currencies before assessing first-month funding, excludes NMD from outflow entirely.

qas.question: Find base USD first-30-day cumulative cash before credit line.
Find base EUR first-30-day cash before facility.
Find minimum USD line draw to meet the base first bucket.
Find EUR cumulative base cash at day90, no line draw.
qas.answer: 30+50−80−100×.1=−10 million USD equivalent; a 10m draw is needed by day90.

qas.question: Find residual USD first-month funding shortfall under stress after full committed line.
Why does positive combined base first-month cash 10 not establish adequate liquidity?
qas.answer: USD is short20 even though EUR has30 surplus; cross-currency transfer prohibited. Currency-specific constraints must be tested.

qas.question: Why not place all nonmaturity deposits outside the maturity ladder?
qas.answer: The toy specifies behavioral withdrawals in both buckets even though no fixed contractual maturity; excluding them understates modeled outflow.

qas.question: Can actual regulatory liquidity ratios be computed from these gap schedules?
qas.answer: No. The toy maturity gap is not a complete regulatory LCR calculation; eligible liquid assets and regulatory runoff rules are missing.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Meadow Lantern Insurance. Toy all premium movements by coverage, no tax/reinstatement. Opening and closing UPR supplied; earned = written + opening UPR−closing UPR separately gross and ceded.

|Property|180|70|60|90|30|40|
|Health|100|30|35|0|0|0|

|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Motor|150|40|45|

[Policy] Net earned premium = gross earned−ceded earned; aggregate combined ratio uses sums of net incurred claims and net underwriting expense divided by net earned premium. No ceding commission outside expenses.

qas.question: Find earned gross motor premium using UPR movement.
Find earned ceded property premium.
Find total net earned premium across all three lines.

qas.question: Find aggregate net incurred claims.
Find aggregate net combined ratio using consistent earned denominator.
Why not average each line's combined ratio with equal weights?
qas.answer: Net earned premiums differ by line. The aggregate ratio weights each line by its own net earned premium rather than treating small and large lines equally.

qas.question: Is net cash collected 490−140 equal to net earned premium?
qas.answer: No. Cash timing and unearned reserves differ from earned coverage; net cash premium350 and net earned370 are distinct.

qas.question: Can the effect of prior-accident-year development on claims be isolated?
qas.answer: No. Only calendar incurred amounts are given; no accident-year development split.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional Birch Current Fund. Toy portfolio assets held unchanged throughout year, local market return and FX compound multiplicatively; hedge gain separately realized. No contributions, fees or taxes.

evidence.text:
[Portfolio opening]
|Asset|USD equivalent|Local market return|FX change vs USD|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|US equities|100|10%|0%|
|EU equities|80|8%|-5%|
|Japan bonds|60|3%|4%|
[FX] Positive FX change means local currency strengthens vs USD. USD growth factor=(1+local return)×(1+FX change). No dividends beyond stated total returns.
[Hedge] Currency forward realized gain3m on EU currency exposure, no other derivative movement. Include in total fund P&L but not individual asset unhedged return.
[NAV] Opening cash10m, unchanged except hedge cash; opening total NAV250. No other flows/expenses.
[Deck] Portfolio manager adds local and FX percentages without interaction, reports EU return3% exactly; adds hedge gain to EU local performance.
[Disclosure] No benchmark or daily return path.

qas.question: Find unhedged USD total return on EU equities.
Find USD value of Japan bonds at year end.
Find total unhedged asset investment gain across three positions.
Find year-end fund NAV including hedge settlement.
Find fund annual net return including hedge, no external flows.
Explain why EU 8%−5%=3% is only an approximation.
qas.answer: Return factors multiply; interaction .08×(−.05)=−.004, so USD return is2.6%, not3%.

qas.question: Should the forward gain be classified as EU local market return?
qas.answer: No. It is distinct currency hedging P&L, not change in the local asset's market value.

qas.answer: No. Notional, hedge timing, targeted exposure and benchmark are not supplied.
